items.text: Gradle wrapper committed with distributionSha256Sum and CI always runs ./gradlew.
Java toolchain set to 25 in the build and CI builds inside the pinned JDK image.
Every library and plugin version in gradle/libs.versions.toml; no version typed in a build file.
Repositories declared only in settings.gradle.kts with repositoriesMode FAIL_ON_PROJECT_REPOS.
BOMs imported with platform() in every configuration that needs them; no io.spring.dependency-management plugin.
Error Prone runs on main code with warnings in generated code disabled.
NullAway as an error with OnlyNullMarked and JSpecifyMode; every package has a package-info.java with @NullMarked.
Spotless with a pinned palantir-java-format; spotlessCheck runs as part of check.
build depends on cyclonedxBom and writes the SBOM to a fixed path.
renovate.json extends config:recommended, sets minimumReleaseAge and groups libraries that must move together.
Dependency update pull requests are reviewed and merged on a green build every week.
One package per business capability under the base package, each a Spring Modulith module with a small API at its root.
A ModulithTest calls ApplicationModules.of(Application.class).verify() in every build.
One style per service, with the same package names in every capability.
Ports, adapters and application services marked with jMolecules hexagonal annotations; port signatures use domain types.
ArchitectureTest runs JMoleculesArchitectureRules.ensureHexagonal(VerificationDepth.STRICT).
An ArchUnit rule that nothing outside the adapter packages depends on them.
An explicit ArchUnit graph for presentation, application, domain and infrastructure in which the domain depends on no other layer.
An ArchUnit rule keeps the domain package to the JDK, JSpecify and itself.
@Transactional only on application service methods, one per use case.
Module boundaries reviewed with the people who know the business whenever a capability is added.
The style was chosen by comparing the consequences on a real scenario and the choice is recorded in an ADR.
Business rules that need tests without a database live in a style whose dependencies point toward the domain.
Each architectural claim is labelled as a definition from a source, a team policy, an executable check or judgment.
Domain classes depend on no Spring type and their tests start no Spring context.
Each adapter has a slice test: @WebMvcTest for controllers, @DataJdbcTest for repositories, @RestClientTest for HTTP clients.
An ApplicationModules.verify() test and an ArchUnit class with the jMolecules rule for the chosen style run in the normal build.
Database tests run against Testcontainers PostgreSQL of the production major version through @ServiceConnection, never a database that runs in memory.
The real migrations run in tests, so a changeset that does not apply fails the build.
Outbound clients are built from Boot's RestClient.Builder and tested with @RestClientTest, error responses included.
Integration tests import one shared @TestConfiguration; no @DirtiesContext and no @MockitoBean in @SpringBootTest classes.
A suite starts the built image with a read-only root filesystem as a user other than root and asserts that /readyz answers 200.
CI runners have Docker for the Testcontainers and image tests.
An OpenAPI 3.1 contract lives in the repository and describes every response, errors included.
openApiGenerate runs the spring generator with interfaceOnly and useSpringBoot4; controllers implement the generated interfaces.
Generated models stay in the web adapter; the domain does not depend on generated code.
spring-boot-starter-validation on the classpath; input rules written in the contract; useSpringBuiltInValidation on.
spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled is true and every error response uses one Problem schema with a stable type URI.
Creates return 201 with Location; a POST retried with the same Idempotency-Key returns the stored result.
Every list endpoint has a default and a maximum limit and rejects a limit above the maximum with 400.
Breaking changes ship as a new version next to the old one; the old version is deprecated with a sunset date before removal.
openApiValidate runs in every build and CI fails a pull request that breaks the contract without a new version.
buf lint and buf breaking against the main branch run in CI for every .proto change.
Deleted fields have their numbers and names reserved; no field number is reused or changes type.
gRPC is served by spring-boot-starter-grpc-server on its own port (9090 by default), apart from the HTTP port.
Every gRPC client channel sets default.deadline.
Exceptions map to specific status codes in one @GrpcAdvice; UNAVAILABLE only when the client may retry.
Retry policies only on methods that are safe to repeat, with every attempt inside the deadline.
Services that serve only gRPC use grpc liveness and readiness probes on the gRPC port.
Server reflection is off in production unless the team relies on it there.
Clients reach gRPC servers through a headless Service with a dns target or through a mesh that balances per call.
spring.grpc.server.keepalive.connection.max-age is set so clients reconnect and spread over new pods.
gRPC observations stay enabled on the server and on every client channel.
gRPC traffic uses TLS from an SSL bundle or mesh mutual TLS; bypass-certificate-validation is never set outside tests.
Connection budget computed: every pool times HPA maximum, surge and draining pods, plus migrations and admin, fits the user connections of each database server.
Fixed pool: maximum-pool-size equals minimum-idle, 10 or less unless measured otherwise.
connection-timeout between 2000 and 5000 ms, max-lifetime below every connection age cap, keepalive-time below network idle timeouts, leak-detection-threshold set.
spring.transaction.default-timeout and spring.jdbc.template.query-timeout set.
Runtime role has statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout.
Separate migration and runtime users; the runtime user cannot change the schema.
Migrations run in a Job before the rollout; the application sets spring.liquibase.enabled to false.
Every schema change reviewed as expand and contract; no rename or drop in the same release as the code change.
Transactional changesets start with SET LOCAL lock_timeout; changesets that ran are never edited.
Integration tests run the real changelog on Testcontainers with the production PostgreSQL major version.
Alerts on hikaricp.connections.pending and hikaricp.connections.timeout.
Point in time restore rehearsed in the last quarter.
The migration Job completes before the rollout starts and a failed Job stops the rollout.
The migration Job has a versioned name (or is recreated by its hook), a low backoffLimit, an activeDeadlineSeconds and a ttlSecondsAfterFinished.
Persistence annotations stay in the persistence adapter; domain classes carry none.
spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto is validate; Liquibase owns the schema.
Every JPA association is LAZY, including @ManyToOne and @OneToOne; each use case loads what it needs with JOIN FETCH, an entity graph or a projection.
hibernate.query.fail_on_pagination_over_collection_fetch is true and hibernate.log_slow_query is set.
spring.jpa.open-in-view is false.
List and search pages read projections; entities are loaded only to be changed.
JDBC batching on (hibernate.jdbc.batch_size, order_inserts, order_updates) and SEQUENCE ids instead of IDENTITY.
No second level cache by default; batch jobs flush and clear the persistence context per chunk.
jOOQ classes are generated in the build from a PostgreSQL container migrated by Liquibase, never edited by hand.
RestClient and HTTP Service Clients for new code; no new RestTemplate usage.
One @ImportHttpServices group per downstream system, with base-url from configuration.
redirects dont-follow for calls between services, plus a status handler that rejects 3xx.
spring.http.clients connect-timeout and read-timeout set globally, tighter per group.
HTTP library chosen explicitly with spring.http.clients.imperative.factory.
Apache pool with maxConnPerRoute at or above the concurrency limit, a connection request timeout of 1 s or less and a connection TTL.
Each attempt is bounded by the client; the retry timeout plus one attempt fits the caller's own timeout.
@EnableResilientMethods present whenever @Retryable or @ConcurrencyLimit is used.
Every @Retryable sets includes, maxRetries of 2 or less, multiplier, jitter and timeout.
Only one layer in the call chain retries a given dependency.
POST and PATCH are retried only with an idempotency key created outside the retry.
@ConcurrencyLimit with policy REJECT on the class for each downstream system, rejection mapped to 503 or 429.
Circuit breaker or rate limiter only with a written reason, using resilience4j-spring-boot4.
Fallbacks never invent business results.
Clients come from Boot builders or HTTP Service groups, with histograms on http.client.requests.
spring.threads.virtual.enabled is true only for I/O bound services; the decision is recorded.
HikariCP maximum-pool-size comes from the database connection budget; connection-timeout is 5 s or less.
Every downstream service has a concurrency limit (@ConcurrencyLimit, Semaphore or bulkhead) and every outbound call has connect and read timeouts.
CPU heavy work runs on a platform pool sized to the cores.
Pod CPU request of at least 1; either -XX:ActiveProcessorCount of at least 2 with no CPU limit or a CPU limit of at least 2.
No custom executor bean silently replaces the virtual thread @Async executor; spring.main.keep-alive is true for apps without a web server.
MDC, security and trace context are propagated across async boundaries; no business logic relies on ThreadLocal caching.
Fan out uses a long lived, context wrapped executor and cancels the tasks that miss the deadline.
A JFR pinning check runs once under load; dashboards show pool pending connections and GC.
Events tied to a database change are written to an outbox table in the same transaction; no direct KafkaTemplate send on that path.
Outbox rows are kept; a cleanup job deletes only rows below the published watermark and older than the retention window.
Publication and replication slot created before the app accepts writes; publication.autocreate.mode filtered; heartbeat.interval.ms set.
max_slot_wal_keep_size set in PostgreSQL and an alert on replication slot lag.
Every event has an Avro schema in the repository, registered from CI; new fields have defaults; no field renamed or removed in place.
Topics created explicitly, one per aggregate type, keyed by aggregate id, with retention longer than the longest incident.
acks and enable.idempotence left at the Kafka defaults (all and true); spring.kafka.template.observation-enabled true.
Consumers store processed event ids in the same transaction as the work and skip duplicates; auto commit off; listener observation enabled.
DefaultErrorHandler with exponential backoff and a DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer; ErrorHandlingDeserializer around the deserializers.
Each dead letter topic has at least as many partitions as its original topic.
Alerts on consumer lag, slot lag and records in dead letter topics; a written replay procedure that has been tried.
RabbitMQ is used for tasks and commands; events that several services read or replay go to Kafka.
Work queues are durable quorum queues (x-queue-type: quorum).
The broker runs at least three nodes.
Queues, exchanges and bindings are declared as beans.
spring.rabbitmq.publisher-confirm-type is correlated, publisher-returns and template.mandatory are true.
Publishers wait on the CorrelationData confirm and treat a nack or a returned message as a failed send.
Listeners acknowledge only after the work is done; prefetch is sized to the time one message takes.
Listener retry is on with a small max-retries and a backoff.
Every work queue has a dead letter exchange with dead-letter-strategy at-least-once and overflow reject-publish.
Messages in dead letter queues are reviewed and replayed or discarded.
Every message has a messageId and consumers skip ids they already processed in the same transaction as the work.
Queues that can fill up have a maximum length and, where old work is useless, a message TTL.
The rabbitmq_prometheus plugin is scraped with alerts on growing depth, queues without consumers and dead lettered messages.
Template and listener observation are enabled.
Every cache has a written reason, a known staleness limit and a measured slow path it replaces.
@EnableCaching sits on its own configuration class and every cache is declared in spring.cache.cache-names.
spring.cache.redis.time-to-live is set; no cache entry lives forever.
Cache values are stored as JSON, keys keep the cache name prefix and carry a version.
The cache manager is transaction aware and writes evict entries after the commit.
Hot keys have spread expiry times and are loaded once per pod.
spring.data.redis.connect-timeout and spring.data.redis.timeout are set far below the request deadline.
A CacheErrorHandler turns cache errors into misses; the service keeps answering when Valkey is down.
Valkey has maxmemory below its container limit and maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru.
Hit ratio, command latency and evicted keys are on a dashboard; cache errors raise an alert.
Memory request equals memory limit.
MaxRAMPercentage set from the table, InitialRAMPercentage equal to it.
GC flag explicit in the ENTRYPOINT (-XX:+UseG1GC unless ZGC or Parallel is documented).
No CPU limit and ActiveProcessorCount equal to the CPU request rounded up, at least 2; with a CPU limit, no ActiveProcessorCount.
ExitOnOutOfMemoryError set; heap dumps only to a volume larger than the heap.
java.io.tmpdir and ErrorFile point at the writable /tmp volume, with ErrorFile on the ENTRYPOINT.
AOT cache built in the image from the extracted layout, without --launcher, with remote calls disabled in the training run.
CI fails the build if the cache is rejected (-XX:AOTMode=on check).
Flags that affect the cache (GC, compact headers) are identical in training and production.
startupProbe budget about three times measured p99 startup on the smallest node type, measured with the AOT cache.
Confirm the heap percentage with Native Memory Tracking under load after each JDK or Boot upgrade.
Single application.yaml with production safe defaults; no dev, qa or prod profiles.
All app settings bound through @ConfigurationProperties records with @Validated, @Valid on nested records and @DefaultValue for defaults.
Secret components guarded against unresolved placeholders, with no other format constraint and toString() overridden.
@ConfigurationPropertiesScan enabled; configuration processor on the annotation processor path.
Per environment values in a versioned ConfigMap loaded with envFrom; a config change triggers a rollout.
enableServiceLinks: false on every pod spec.
Secrets in a vault, mounted by the CSI driver with a workload identity; spring.config.import: optional:configtree:...
No secretObjects sync unless something other than the app needs a Kubernetes Secret.
Token authentication preferred over stored secrets for databases and cloud services.
Secret rotation runbook: add the new credential, update the vault, roll the pods, revoke the old one.
management.endpoint.env.show-values and configprops.show-values are never or a SanitizingFunction bean exists.
Only health and info exposed over the web, on the management port.
No secret in manifests, images, ConfigMaps, logs or exception messages.
An invalid setting makes the application context fail to start.
Feature flags evaluated through OpenFeature with safe defaults; stale flags removed.
spring-boot-starter-opentelemetry on the classpath; no -javaagent and no agent injected through JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.
spring.application.name, service.version and deployment.environment.name set.
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT points at the collector in each environment.
management.tracing.sampling.probability chosen deliberately (1.0 with tail sampling).
management.otlp.metrics.export.base-time-unit is seconds.
Histograms on http.server.requests and http.client.requests; explicit SLO buckets for SLI thresholds.
No unbounded tag values; HTTP clients use URI templates and auto-configured builders only.
Logback OpenTelemetry appender installed or stdout JSON collected by an agent, not both.
A collector gateway with memory limiter first, Kubernetes metadata, PII transform, tail sampling, batch and retry.
Grafana data sources linked from exemplars to traces, traces to logs and metrics and logs back to traces.
Actuator on port 8081, exposure limited to health and info (plus prometheus when scraped), health details hidden.
No NetworkPolicy rule admits port 8081.
issuer-uri and audiences set; jws-algorithms explicit.
scp mapped to SCOPE_ and roles to ROLE_; oid as the principal; the API registration issues v2 tokens.
The API chain ends with anyRequest().denyAll(); business rules use @PreAuthorize; a catch-all handler rethrows security exceptions.
Stateless sessions; CSRF off only because no endpoint uses cookie authentication; CORS with exact origins or none.
Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy and HSTS present on responses through the ingress.
server.forward-headers-strategy pinned; server.tomcat.remoteip.internal-proxies narrowed to the ingress addresses.
spring.web.error.* at defaults; spring.mvc.problemdetails.enabled true; a catch-all handler returns a fixed text.
Validation 400s carry errors with field and message, never the rejected value; request sizes bounded on purpose.
URLs that users supply go through a client with InetAddressFilter.externalAddresses(), no redirects and https only.
Pod runs non-root with a read-only root filesystem and /tmp emptyDir, drops ALL capabilities, uses RuntimeDefault and mounts no service account token.
The namespace enforces Pod Security restricted; a NetworkPolicy denies by default with explicit allows and blocks 169.254.169.254.
Where TLS ends is written down: at the ingress, in the pod or in a mesh.
TLS in the pod or mTLS to a partner uses a named SSL bundle; server bundles set reload-on-update: true.
Certificate Secrets mounted as directories, not with subPath; pods rolled when a client certificate is renewed.

guides.title: The container image and supply chain

items.text: Dockerfile with several stages; no JDK, Gradle or source code in the final image.
extract --layers without --launcher; layers copied dependencies, loader, snapshots, application.
AOT cache trained in the runtime stage with remote calls disabled; CI fails if -XX:AOTMode=on rejects it.
Base images pinned as tag@sha256:digest in plain FROM lines with the distro codename in the tag, auxiliary images included.
Every workload running the app image (Deployment, migration Job, CronJob) references the release digest, not a tag.
Renovate or Dependabot updates base digests and action SHAs; JDK major bumps blocked.
Numeric non-root USER 10001:10001 and exec form ENTRYPOINT.
Runs with readOnlyRootFilesystem: true and /tmp as an emptyDir with a sizeLimit.
Allow list .dockerignore; no secrets through ARG or ENV.
CycloneDX plugin applied; app SBOM written by the build. /actuator/sbom not exposed by default; if it is, management port only and authenticated.
Image SBOM (Syft, CycloneDX) attached as a signed attestation.
Trivy or Grype gate on fixable high and critical findings in CI; a registry or cluster scanner rescans shipped images.
Image signed by digest in CI; Deployments reference digests; an admission policy verifies the signature.
Every action and reusable workflow is pinned to a full commit SHA with its version in a comment or locked by a workflow lockfile.
Every workflow starts with permissions contents read; write permissions are granted per job and only where needed.
The repository or organization default for the workflow token is read only.
No pull_request_target or workflow_run workflow checks out and runs pull request code while holding secrets.
The Gradle build runs inside the JDK image pinned by digest, the same digest as the Dockerfile's build stage.
The Gradle wrapper sets distributionSha256Sum.
No secret, token or credential is written to a cached path; caches are keyed by lock or version files.
The image is built from the production Dockerfile and behaviour tests run against it before anything is published.
Test reports upload with if always and the publishing job needs the test job.
Images are pushed and deployed by digest, with a provenance attestation and an SBOM attached to that digest.
Pull request runs never publish; only the default branch does.
Every workflow has paths filters that include the workflow file, a concurrency group per ref and timeout-minutes on every job.
No path filtered workflow is a required status check.
Renovate pull requests for actions, images and libraries are reviewed and merged when CI passes, after the minimum release age.
/livez and /readyz served on the main port (add-additional-paths) and open to the kubelet without authentication.
Liveness group holds livenessState only; no database, broker or HTTP dependency.
Readiness group holds readinessState; any added dependency is local to the pod and documented.
Probe timeoutSeconds is at least 2; startupProbe instead of initialDelaySeconds.
preStop sleep of at least 10 s with the native sleep action.
timeout-per-shutdown-phase set to 20s and terminationGracePeriodSeconds at least preStop plus the phase timeout plus 15 s.
Memory request equals memory limit; CPU request set and no CPU limit or a documented reason for one.
maxSurge 1, maxUnavailable 0 and minReadySeconds set; no spec.replicas when an autoscaler exists.
PodDisruptionBudget with maxUnavailable 1 and unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy AlwaysAllow.
HorizontalPodAutoscaler with explicit behavior and a capped scale up; minReplicas at least 3 in production; one autoscaler per Deployment.
Zone spread with DoNotSchedule and node spread with ScheduleAnyway, both with matchLabelKeys pod-template-hash.
Recurring work uses ShedLock or a CronJob with concurrencyPolicy Forbid.
A rollout under steady load has finished with zero failed requests at least once.
A pod that is not ready is diagnosed from its events, kubectl logs --previous and a direct call to /livez and /readyz.

guides.title: Kubernetes manifests: plain, Helm or Kustomize

items.text: One packaging tool per service: Kustomize for a service the team deploys itself, Helm when others install it with their own values. The choice is written down.
CI renders every environment and validates the rendered output, not the templates.
Recommended app.kubernetes.io labels on every object. Selectors use name, instance and component only, never version.
No spec.replicas in any manifest when an HPA manages the Deployment.
Production images pinned by digest through the Kustomize images transformer.
Config changes roll the pods: configMapGenerator hash or checksum/config. Plain YAML has an explicit restart step.
Kustomize uses labels, patches and replacements only, with components for optional features. No deprecated fields.
Applied with --server-side and a named field manager. Drift checked with kubectl diff --server-side or a GitOps controller.
kubeconform -strict with CRD schemas for Kubernetes 1.36 and 1.37, plus pluto for the newest version.
kube-linter and trivy config pass. Every suppression has a written reason.
With more than one person deploying or more than one cluster, a GitOps controller applies the manifests with pruning on.
Dependencies such as a migration before the app are ordered explicitly: Argo CD sync waves or Flux dependsOn.
Local dependencies run in containers with the image versions production runs; no embedded database stands in for PostgreSQL.
spring-boot-docker-compose is a developmentOnly dependency and compose.yml sits next to the app, with a healthcheck per service.
No connection URL, user or password for a local container appears in application.yaml; service connections provide them.
Containers are started one way only, Docker Compose support or Testcontainers at development time, never both.
grafana/otel-lgtm 0.37.0 runs locally for traces, metrics and logs and never in a shared or production environment.
Every setting uses the same key locally and in the cluster, with local defaults as placeholders overridden by environment variables.
spring-boot-devtools is a developmentOnly dependency and never reaches the image.
Every environment except local sets spring.liquibase.contexts to a value without dev, so sample data changesets never run there.
Probes, mounts and policies are checked in a local cluster before manifests change.
pyahu.yaml lists the services the project needs, so pyahu up starts the same local stack for every developer.
The decision to keep several services in one repository is recorded in an ADR with its reason and the owning team.
No service has a project dependency on another service; services share only contracts and generated client projects.
Each service owns its database and its migration history.
libs/ holds only deliberately reusable code, never shared entities or service internals.
Each contract lives in contracts/<service>/ with the producing service as owner.
CI compares every contract with its last released version and fails on a breaking change.
Build logic lives in an included build-logic build, added with includeBuild inside pluginManagement; no buildSrc, allprojects or subprojects.
Convention plugins have their own Gradle TestKit tests.
One version catalog at gradle/libs.versions.toml, imported into build-logic.
Each service is included by a flat project name with an explicit projectDir; the root project has no sources.
One orchestration workflow that always runs ends in a gate job that is the only required check.
Each service has its own image repository, built from the repository root and its own deploy/ folder.
The same image digest is promoted between environments; releases are tagged per service.
Data fetching and service calls live in server components; modules that hold secrets or call the service start with import 'server-only'.
The TypeScript client types are generated from the service's OpenAPI document and CI fails when the generated file is out of date.
The browser never calls the service directly; the Next.js server calls it by its cluster name.
Login runs the OIDC code flow on the server with a maintained library; the session is an httpOnly, secure, sameSite cookie and the access token never reaches the browser.
Every Server Action and every data access function checks the user itself, not only proxy.ts.
One image is promoted across environments; no environment specific value uses the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix.
Nothing that depends on the user's session is cached in a shared cache; cached reads have a tag and a lifetime.
With more than one replica, cached data uses a shared cache handler or a short lifetime per pod.
The image is built with output: 'standalone', copies only .next/standalone, .next/static and public, runs as the node user and starts with CMD ["node", "server.js"].
Probes point at a route handler that returns 200; the grace period covers the slowest request; several replicas share the Server Actions encryption key and a deploymentId.
next.config.js sets nosniff, a referrer policy, frame denial and HSTS on every path, poweredByHeader is false and a Content Security Policy is in place.
instrumentation.ts registers OpenTelemetry with the service's address in fetch.propagateContextUrls and exports to the same collector as the service.
